'''Jeremy Henley Burroughes''' {{post-nominals|size=100%|country=GBR|FREng|FRS}} (born August 1960) is a British [[physicist]] and [[engineer]], known for his contributions to the development of [[organic electronics]] through his work on the science of [[semiconducting]] [[polymer]]s and [[molecule]]s and their application.<ref name="FRS" /> He is the Chief Technology Officer of [[Cambridge Display Technology]], a company specialising in the development of technologies based on [[polymer light-emitting diode]]s.

==Education==
Burroughes earned his PhD from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1989.<ref name="Edwards2008">{{cite book|author=Steven A. Edwards|title=The Nanotech Pioneers: Where Are They Taking Us|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KqoZ2e1waogC&pg=PA117|date=8 January 2008|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-3-527-61209-3|pages=117–118}}</ref> His thesis was entitled ''The physical processes in organic semiconducting polymer devices.''<ref name="bl">[http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?did=1&uin=uk.bl.ethos.306360 British Library EthOS], retrieved 2016-03-26.</ref>

== Work ==
Early in his career, Burroughes discovered that certain [[conjugated polymer]]s were capable of emitting [[light]] when an [[electric current]] passed through them. The discovery of this previously unknown form of [[electroluminescence]] led to the foundation of Cambridge Display Technology where Burroughes has been responsible for a number of technology innovations, including the direct printing of full-colour [[OLED display]]s.<ref name="FRS" />

== Awards and honours ==
Burroughes was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2012|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2012]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jeremy-burroughes-11173 |title=Jeremy Burroughes |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |location=London }} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." {{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220093712/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=20 February 2016 }}</ref> His certificate of election reads: {{centered pull quote|Burroughes made the seminal advances in the science and engineering of semiconducting polymers that have brought these materials from research to the marketplace. His early papers from Cambridge on polymer [[Field-effect transistor|FETs]] (1988) and [[Light-emitting diode|LEDs]] (1990) defined the scope of the field. In his role as Chief Technology Officer at Cambridge Display Technology he has transformed early demonstration into fully [[manufacturing|manufacturable]] technology, using new device architectures, new materials and new manufacturing processes such as direct printing of full colour LED displays. This engineering programme has generated fundamental understanding of the underlying device physics.<ref name="frsCitation">{{cite web|url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%27EC%2F2012%2F06%27%29|title=EC/2012/06: Burroughes, Jeremy Henley|publisher=[[The Royal Society]]|accessdate=26 March 2016|archive-date=5 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305030444/https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%27EC%2F2012%2F06%27%29|url-status=dead}}</ref>}}
